note: Both sets capture the same core facts correctly: the 27 in./68.6 cm TV display minimum, the 15 in./38.1 cm computer display minimum, the 75%-of-maximum TV brightness requirement, the simultaneous/independent operation requirement, and the eight-person dinner minimum with its guest breakdown. Neither set contains any misread, misbound or invented claim. However, both repeat the same display-size facts under multiple attribute names (inches and centimeters, 'minimum size' and 'minimum manufacturer stated display size'), and B adds two further duplicates of these same facts beyond A's, giving B more redundancy without adding any new correct content. A is therefore marginally better as the leaner set of equally correct claims.
remarks: Both extractions state each display-size limit four times (in./cm x 'minimum size'/'minimum manufacturer stated display size') and the brightness limit twice; a normalization step that merges unit-variant and attribute-synonym duplicates would help. Both sets also omit several facts on the page that could be extracted, e.g. the computer may be a laptop or desktop, there is no required volume setting, organizers supply the TV and computer content, and the safety rules in 9-3k (no flames, no alcohol, sealed drinking water, coolers prohibited on site). The brightness condition 'of maximum' in the second brightness claim is a fragment of the requirement rather than a real condition.
